skills.description: Forges reusable Skill packages (SKILL.md + scripts) from website exploration via browser-act — no re-exploration later. Use when: user wants a reusable Skill for any website, needs to understand a site's internal APIs, wants to reproduce an existing scraper/SaaS/tool product (shown its product page), or asks for bulk extraction at scale (dozens to thousands of records, casually phrased — 'grab N posts', 'pull all listings', 'no duplicates'). Unlike browser-act: reusable, not one-off. Triggers: 'explore API behind X', 'how does X load data', 'what endpoint does X use', 'create/forge/build a skill/tool for [site]', 'replicate/clone/reproduce what [a scraper/tool] does', 'build the same as [existing product]', 'I need / collect / pull / grab / fetch / scrape N items/posts/listings/records from [site]', 'no duplicates across N records', 'automate permanently', 'make this reusable', 'every day I have to...', 'monitor [site]', 'browser-act-skill-forge'. The next session verifies predictions against actual outcomes, and a validation gate accepts edits only when improvement is measurable. Runs automatically on harvest-loop Step 0-c and on explicit invocation.

skills.name: fh
skills.description: Renders the FH hub map on demand — the door menu, a starter set of skills, and the most-used trigger phrases — without requiring a greeting. State-aware; composes live candidates from the session card and tracks.

skills.name: field-harvest
skills.description: Scans git history of field projects to detect patterns worth backporting to the meta-harness (Mode A), and logs session work to the knowledge hub when a session ends (Mode B). Triggers on "save this pattern", "make this reusable across projects", "can we automate this repetition?", "push this to FH", "reverse absorption", "harvest pattern", "session log", "log today's work", "sync to hub".

skills.name: frontier-digest
skills.description: Collects the latest AI/harness engineering trends from HackerNews, arxiv, launch channels (Launch YC, Product Hunt, Show HN), GeekNews and vendor changelogs, then synthesizes them into actionable insights directly relevant to forge-harness operations. Triggered by "AI trends", "latest trends", "this week's AI updates", "what's on the frontier", "harness trends", "frontier-digest".

skills.name: goal-quench
skills.description: Wraps /goal with a tiered safety + orchestration ladder. core (default): a token budget gate (pre-run estimate), mid-run budget thresholds, and an automatic post-run quality verification via pipeline-conductor — closing /goal's two gaps (the runner's per-turn judge evaluates completion, pipeline-conductor evaluates correctness). pro: adds context-doctor token reduction and agent-composer goal decomposition. max: adds internal-first capability-gap fill (LOCAL_SKILL_REGISTRY skill-bus scan → plugin-recommender external search → auto_project_mapping map/cluster) and cross-ecosystem-synergy-detection pre-validation. The Phase-1 budget verdict auto-recommends the mode. Triggered by "goal with quality gate", "safe goal", "goal-quench", "orchestrate this goal", or before running /goal on high-stakes tasks.

skills.name: harness-pr-reviewer
skills.description: Checks a submitted PR against the environment's baseline assets (CLAUDE.md, memory, naming, asset classification) and attaches a review comment with a merge recommendation. 5 steps — diff read, 8-area consistency check, self-catch, comment, merge recommendation.

skills.name: harvest-loop
skills.description: An 8-step self-evolution pipeline that runs after field sessions end (field-harvest → contention-layer → challenger + persona-innovator → synthesizer → Critic agent → harness-doctor → verify-bidirectional → curator), absorbing session learnings back into the FH ecosystem. Runs automatically at session end in the main dev environment; proposes execution first for external users. Triggered by "session harvest", "learning absorption", "fh evolution", or "harvest-loop". (The phrase "run the pipeline" is ceded to pipeline-conductor — use that for end-to-end verification sweeps.)

skills.name: install-doctor
skills.description: Scans the existing environment (after the built-in `/doctor` — this covers FH-plugin conflicts it does not) before and after meta-harness plugin install to diagnose conflicts, duplicates, and silent overwrite risks. Reports potential conflict areas with existing CLAUDE.md, skills, hooks, and audit practices. Activates on "install conflict", "any overlaps?", "is it safe to install?".

skills.name: ko-tech-writer
skills.description: Writes or revises Korean technical prose across three registers — reader-facing documents (tech-blog posts, technical docs), spoken scripts, and derived compressed assets (teasers, summaries) — through a fixed pipeline: register detection, real-sample calibration of the target venue, a translationese-removal pass, honesty-level layering (reader information vs internal audit vocabulary), a number/claim gate, and a rendition + perceptual QA pass. Triggers: "기술문서 써줘", "테크블로그 초안 잡아줘", "이 문서 번역투 고쳐줘", "블로그체로 다듬어줘", "이 글 회사 기술블로그에 올릴 수 있게 다듬어줘", "발표 대본 다듬어줘", "낭독 대본 점검해줘", "이 스크립트 소리 내서 읽을 때 걸리는 데 있나".

skills.name: marketplace-gate
skills.description: Evaluates whether a repository meets marketplace listing criteria via a 5-point check and outputs a listing suitability verdict. Checks README completeness, zero-config readiness, maintenance signals, duplication, and public safety.

skills.name: mcp-circuit-breaker
skills.description: Detects MCP tool failure patterns and trips a circuit breaker to stop cascading retries. Proposes fallback alternatives and resets when the tool recovers. Triggers on "MCP failing", "tool keeps erroring", "circuit-breaker", repeated tool call failures.

skills.name: memory-hygiene
skills.description: Detects "stale-but-confident" memory entries — facts that were once verified but have silently drifted. Scans memory/*.md for entries past their staleness threshold and proposes re-verification or archival. Runs automatically as part of harvest-loop Step 0-c and on explicit invocation.

skills.name: meta-prompt-builder
skills.description: Generates structured prompts to send to each agent in an agent dispatch plan. Triggered by "write the instructions", "what do I say to the agent?", "write the prompt for me", "meta-prompt-builder". Bridges agent-composer (which agents) and prompt content (what to say). Uses Goal/Context/Constraints/Done When structure.

skills.name: persona-cast
skills.description: One-line doorway that lets a field harness review an artifact (a screen, a spec, a PR, a page) through a pre-built cast of review-shaped personas — web-review cast by default (designer, ux-writer, fe-dev, be-dev, qa, a11y) — dispatched in isolation, merged with a marginal-coverage stop so a lens that finds nothing unique is reported as decorative, not padded. Triggers: "이 화면 리뷰해줘", "페르소나로 봐줘", "디자이너·QA 눈으로 봐줘", "review this screen with the cast", "persona cast", "persona-cast".

skills.name: persona-roster-expander
skills.description: Expands a named persona seed into a tiered, judgment-mapped cast — tiering each persona by a domain safety rule, mapping each to a decision-lens in the user's vocabulary, then proposing additional voices with sourced anchors.

skills.name: phantom-quench
skills.description: Input-tracing grounding audit for artifacts such as test cases, analysis reports, and design docs. Extracts proper nouns, numbers, citations, version claims, and branching conditions, then back-traces each to declared local files by grep or to external sources by fetch-and-support checks. Marks missing anchors as Phantom Claims and cited-but-unsupporting anchors as Unsupported. A claim is grounded only by non-model evidence: a local hit or literal source span, never another model's agreement. Renamed from source-grounding-audit; old-name references still route here. Triggered by: "phantom detection", "phantom claim", "source back-trace", "where did this come from", "verify source", "does the source support this claim", "grounding audit", "source grounding audit", "citation support check".

skills.name: pipeline-conductor
skills.description: Chains the four core FH verification pipelines (harvest-loop → steel-quench → phantom-quench → sim-conductor) into a single gated sweep. Accepts a scope (single skill, specific asset, full harness) and aggregates results into one structured report. Supports --quick mode (steps 2+3 only) and --full mode (all four steps). Triggered by "run the full pipeline", "chain all verifications", "end-to-end sweep", "pipeline-conductor", or "verify everything".

skills.name: prompt-regression
skills.description: Statically checks harness assets against a known-answer probe set after rule/skill changes — inspects the changed source for the trigger phrases, chain links and gate conditions each probe expects, and reports PASS/FAIL/SKIP per probe. Source inspection only; it does not run live sessions, so it catches assets that no longer SAY the right thing, not models that stop DOING it. Triggers on "prompt regression", "did my changes break anything", "regression check", "test harness changes".

skills.name: public-surface-audit
skills.description: Scans git-tracked (public) files for operator-private tokens that should live only in gitignored files — real usernames, absolute home paths, companion-store names, company asset names. Reports file:line + matched token + severity, so a public/private split stays clean before publish. Triggered by "public surface audit", "did I leak anything", "check tracked files for private tokens", "private token scan", "public-surface-audit".

skills.name: qp
skills.description: QP (Quality Platform) router — takes a web URL or a desktop app name and runs the plan → run → regress loop (qp-plan, qp-run, qp-regress) end to end, or routes to one stage. Classifies the target (public vs profile-required), probes which adapter the session has (Playwright MCP for web, computer-use MCP for desktop), and writes every artifact with a typed engine/adapter marker. Triggers on "test this website for me", "run a QA pass on this app", "check the app end to end", "이 사이트 QA 돌려줘", "이 앱 테스트해줘", "회귀 돌려줘".

skills.name: qp-plan
skills.description: Prepare stage of QP — builds a surface inventory of a web page or desktop app (routes, menus, forms, dialogs), checks it is MECE (no overlap, nothing missing that is visible), and designs test cases as a TSV with preconditions and expected values whose SOURCE is named. Works without a spec document (then expected values come from the inventory, not a plan). Triggers on "what should I test on this page", "make a test plan for this app", "list the screens of this app", "테스트 케이스 뽑아줘", "이 화면 인벤토리 만들어줘".

skills.name: qp-regress
skills.description: Regression stage of QP — re-executes a previous run's test cases unchanged, computes surface_reach (how many TCs left the entry screen, as a ratio over ALL TCs), and reports the per-TC delta against the earlier run so a "no change" claim is per case, not an aggregate. Triggers on "did anything regress since last run", "re-run last week's QA pass", "compare this run with the previous one", "회귀 확인해줘", "지난 런이랑 비교해줘".

skills.name: qp-run
skills.description: Automation stage of QP — executes the test cases from qp-plan against the live app through the session's adapter (Playwright MCP for web, computer-use MCP for desktop), records one verdict per step with a closed status, an MTM branch, whether the step was closed by machine evidence or left to judgment, and masks emails/tokens/passwords out of the evidence before saving. Triggers on "run these test cases", "execute the QA plan against the site", "drive the app through the TCs", "TC 실행해줘", "플랜대로 돌려줘".

skills.name: return-path-gate
skills.description: Audits SKILL.md files in plugins/ for return-path gate compliance. Detects fire-and-forget chains where a caller dispatches a downstream skill but does not gate its next step on the callee's verdict. Reports each chain as CLOSED or OPEN and outputs specific fix suggestions. Triggered by "chain audit", "return-path check", "fire-and-forget detection", "chain closure audit", "skill chain compliance".

skills.name: salience-splitter
skills.description: Splits an over-loaded always-loaded context asset (SKILL.md, CLAUDE.md, memory index) into a lean resident layer plus an on-demand layer, by when content is needed rather than by length, linked by imperative pointers. Alias: skill-splitter. Triggers: "SKILL.md too large", "split this skill", "skill is bloated", "skill file too long", "CLAUDE.md 너무 커".

skills.name: sim-conductor
skills.description: Autonomously runs external user reaction simulations, internal audits, ideation scans, artifact validation, and quality reviews. Profiles the target artifact first, then derives task-appropriate personas, dispatches them as parallel agents, classifies findings into M/S/R tiers, and completes the pipeline through to commit automatically.

skills.name: standpoint-review
skills.description: Standpoint review — check a change from the side that RECEIVES it: copy the receiving repo (or a clean install of the package) into an isolated folder, apply the change there, run that repo's OWN checks, have a reviewer judge the change against that repo's OWN rules with none of the author's explanation, then verify every finding against the source before acting on it. Use when asked whether a change breaks, or still works with, another repo, app, harness or package consumer that depends on it. Triggers: "입장 리뷰", "받는 쪽에서 돌려 봐", "하위 레포에서 돌려 봐", "그 레포 규칙으로 검증해 줘", "standpoint review", "run it from the target", "check it from the downstream repo", "make sure it won't break the repo that depends on it", "will this change break downstream users".

skills.name: token-budget-gate
skills.description: Estimates token cost before a multi-step task and outputs a 4-tier Green/Yellow/Orange/Red gate verdict. Records actual vs. estimated after completion when a mechanical usage source exists. Triggers on "token budget", "how much will this cost", "will this be expensive", "estimate tokens", before long multi-agent tasks.

skills.name: verify-bidirectional
skills.description: A skill that immediately updates the baseline and reflects it in the next session when the user raises a counter-argument to an AI recommendation. Triggered by "is that right?", "re-examine this", "something seems off here". Explicit /verify-bidirectional call also possible.

skills.name: video-ingest
skills.description: Ingests a video's content (YouTube and similar) for agent context, routing by capability, task need, and video length — a natively multimodal engine (Gemini via agy or the Gemini API) for direct-URL and long video, Claude vision over ffmpeg-extracted frames when no such engine is present, yt-dlp captions when the transcript alone suffices, and the logged-in claude-in-chrome session for auth-gated videos. The governor cross-checks any multimodal comprehensive-read. Triggered by "ingest this video", "what does this video show", "get the transcript from this YouTube video", "video-ingest".

plugins.name: frontend-craft-skills
plugins.description: Fourteen skills for interface craft: animation vocabulary and performance, reviewing animations, gestures, Apple-style design, native mobile and Swift work, picking a UI library and learning taste.
plugins.author: Emil Kowalski
exampleQueries: Review this animation for performance
Add a gesture to this screen
Which UI library fits this app?

skills.name: animate
skills.description: Build an animation from scratch, making the decisions in the order that determines whether it feels right — should it animate at all, what purpose, which tool, which properties, which curve and duration, how it interrupts, how it exits. Writes the implementation. Use when asked to animate something, add motion, make a component feel alive, or build a transition. For critiquing existing motion use review-animations; for auditing a whole codebase use improve-animations.

skills.name: animate-expo
skills.description: Build animations in React Native and Expo, making the decisions in the order that determines whether they feel right — should it animate, which thread it runs on, which properties, spring or timing, how the gesture hands off, how it degrades. Writes the implementation with Reanimated, Gesture Handler, Expo Router and expo-haptics. Use when animating anything in an Expo app, adding gestures, sheets, screen transitions, press feedback or haptics, or fixing motion that stutters on device. For web animation use `animate`.

skills.name: animation-performance
skills.description: Keep web animations inside the frame budget — animate composite-only properties, keep motion off the main thread when the page is busy, and find the cause when an animation drops frames. Use when an animation is janky, choppy, stutters, or drops frames; when choosing which property to animate; when deciding between CSS and JS animation on performance grounds; or when reaching for `will-change` or GPU layers. For choosing easing, duration, or whether to animate at all use animate; for reviewing motion as a whole use review-animations.

skills.name: animation-vocabulary
skills.description: Reverse-lookup glossary that turns a vague description of a web animation or motion effect into its exact term ("the bouncy thing when a popover opens" → Pop in; "the iOS rubber-band scroll" → Rubber-banding). Use when the user asks "what's it called when…", or describes a motion effect without knowing its name and wants the right word to prompt an AI or designer with. For naming an effect, not designing or building one.

skills.name: apple-design
skills.description: Apple's approach to interface design and fluid, physical motion, translated for the web. Use when building or reviewing gesture-driven UI, spring animations, drag/swipe/sheet interactions, momentum and interruptible transitions, translucent materials and depth, typography (optical sizing, tracking, leading), reduced-motion, or the design foundations (feedback, spatial consistency, restraint) behind Apple-style interfaces.

skills.name: ask-emil
skills.description: Ask which skill or flow fits your situation. A router over the skills in this repo.

skills.name: ask-sonner
skills.description: Guide to Sonner, the React toast library — install and wire up the Toaster, pick the right toast() call, promise and loading toasts, updating, dismissing and persisting toasts, styling, theming and icons, positioning and multiple toasters. Use when working with Sonner or troubleshooting it — toasts that don't appear, appear twice, lose their styles, ignore Tailwind classes, sit behind a modal, or don't follow dark mode.

skills.name: emil-design-eng
skills.description: Emil Kowalski's design-engineering philosophy for UI polish, component design, animation decisions, and the invisible details that make software feel great. Use when building or reviewing a UI component's interactions and polish (press and hover states, popover origin, tooltip timing, transitions vs keyframes, clip-path techniques, drag details) and no narrower skill fits.

skills.name: gestures
skills.description: Build drag, swipe, and sheet interactions that track the finger 1:1 and stay interruptible. Use when building or fixing anything the user drags, swipes, flings, holds, or dismisses with a gesture — drawers, sheets, swipe-to-dismiss toasts and cards, drag-to-reorder, pull-to-refresh, hold-to-confirm — or when a gesture feels laggy, disconnected from the finger, jumps on release, or can't be caught mid-animation. Triggers on — gesture, drag, swipe, fling, sheet, snap points, Vaul, Motion drag props, rubber-band, pull to refresh, hold to delete, touch-action, "doesn't follow my finger", "jumps when I let go", "can't grab it mid-animation".

skills.name: learn-taste
skills.description: Turn a session's design corrections into rules, with their why, in DESIGN.md, a project skill, or a lint check.

skills.name: mobile-native
skills.description: Make a web app feel native on a phone — the small CSS and meta-tag fixes that separate "a website in a browser" from something that feels installed. Covers sticky hover states, tap highlight flashes, the 100vh bug, inputs that zoom the page, laggy taps, pull-to-refresh hijacking scroll, content under the notch, long-press selecting button text, carousels that scroll the wrong way, mismatched status bars, and the rule that you test on real hardware. Use when a web app is being built for or reviewed on mobile, when something "works in Chrome but feels wrong on my phone", when building a PWA, a bottom sheet, a carousel, a full-screen layout, or any touch interaction. For motion itself use animate; for React Native use animate-expo.

skills.name: pick-ui-library
skills.description: Pick the library for a frontend task from a curated list — primitives, toasts, drawers, command menus, OTP, numbers, charts, virtualization, drag and drop, state, styling.

skills.name: review-animations
skills.description: Reviews animation and motion code against a high craft bar derived from Emil Kowalski's design engineering philosophy. Default to flagging; approval is earned.

skills.name: write-swift
skills.description: How to write modern Swift well — modeling with value types, Swift 6 data-race safety and approachable concurrency (@concurrent, main-actor-by-default, actors, task groups), protocols and generics (some vs any), API design, performance and ARC, Swift Testing, macros, and the modern language features agents don't know about yet. Use when writing, reviewing, or migrating Swift, or when a concurrency error, a hang, a data race, a retain cycle, or a performance problem needs fixing.

plugins.name: game-development-skills
plugins.description: Sixty-three skills for game development: AI behaviour trees and utility AI, camera systems, audio, dialogue, card games, FPS and Bevy ECS.
plugins.author: gamedev-skills
exampleQueries: Write the behaviour tree for this enemy
Set up the camera in this game
How do I structure this Bevy ECS?

skills.name: ai-behavior-trees-utility-ai
skills.description: Engine-neutral behavior tree and utility AI code for NPCs in any language: Blackboard, reactive composites, decorators and response-curve scoring. Use when an enemy keeps chasing after losing sight, restarts its action every frame or flip-flops between choices. Not for FSMs, steering or pathfinding (`game-ai`) or Unreal BT, EQS and StateTree (`unreal-behavior-trees`).

skills.name: audio-design
skills.description: Engine-neutral game audio technique: bus layout, volume sliders in decibels, loudness, ducking music under dialogue, adaptive music and SFX variation, with Godot, Unity and FMOD/Wwise mappings. Use when mixing a game, making music react to combat, fixing repetitive footsteps or beat sync, or a mix that clips or pumps. Not for the Godot audio API (`godot-audio`).

skills.name: bevy-ecs
skills.description: Builds and debugs Bevy 0.20 games in Rust: components, Query and Commands systems, schedules, States, observers and headless tests. Use when Cargo.toml depends on bevy, on a B0001 query-conflict panic, or pre-0.20 code (EventReader, SpriteBundle). Not for engine-neutral AI, generation, physics or shaders (`game-ai`, `procedural-gen`, `physics-tuning`, `shader-programming`).

skills.name: camera-systems
skills.description: Builds and tunes game cameras, engine-neutral with Godot and Cinemachine 3 mappings: 2D follow with deadzone and look-ahead, third-person orbit, first-person look and split-screen. Use when the camera lags, jitters while following, shows past the level edge, clips through walls or changes with frame rate. Not for shake (`game-feel`) or physics timestep jitter (`physics-tuning`).

skills.name: card-game
skills.description: Designs card games and deckbuilders in any engine: cards as data with one effect interpreter, deck zones, a trigger stack and seeded shuffles. Use for a Slay the Spire- or Balatro-like or a TCG, or cards that duplicate or streaky shuffles. Pair with the engine skill for card data and hand UI (`godot-resources`, `godot-ui-control`, `unity-scriptableobjects`). Not for grid crawlers (`roguelike`).

skills.name: dialogue-systems
skills.description: Builds engine-neutral branching dialogue with Ink, Yarn Spinner or a small JSON graph runner: lines, choices, conditions, variables and localization IDs. Use for NPC conversations, dialogue trees, barks, .ink or .yarn files, or dialogue that dead-ends. Not for visual-novel backlog and skip (`visual-novel`), quests (`rpg`) or text box widgets (`godot-ui-control`, `game-ui-ux`).

skills.name: fps-shooter
skills.description: Designs first-person shooter combat in any engine: hitscan vs projectiles, time-to-kill, damage falloff, recoil patterns, ADS sensitivity and lag-compensated hits. Use for a Doom- or Counter-Strike-like, or guns that feel weak or shots that do not register. Not for the camera rig (`camera-systems`), shake and hit-stop (`game-feel`) or raycast APIs (`godot-physics`, `unity-physics`).

skills.name: game-ai
skills.description: Designs engine-neutral enemy and NPC AI: picks FSM, behavior tree, utility or GOAP, and builds perception, steering and A* pathfinding. Use for patrol and chase, "find a path to the player", agents stuck on corners or AI that sees through walls. Not for BT or utility code (`ai-behavior-trees-utility-ai`), Unreal AI (`unreal-behavior-trees`) or Unity NavMesh (`unity-navmesh`).

skills.name: game-feel
skills.description: Adds engine-neutral juice to a working mechanic: trauma-based screen shake, hit-stop, eased tweens, squash and stretch, and knockback. Use when the game feels flat, weightless or not punchy, or hits and jumps should feel satisfying. Not for coyote time (`platformer`), input buffering (`input-systems`), camera follow (`camera-systems`) or HUD layout (`game-ui-ux`).

skills.name: game-jam
skills.description: Plans and ships a game jam entry against a fixed deadline: reads the jam rules, scopes to the clock, keeps a cut list and checks the build before submitting. Use for Ludum Dare, GMTK, Global Game Jam or any itch.io jam, a 48-hour game, or "we're behind, what do we cut". Not for untimed experiments (`prototype-fast`) or upload commands (`itch-publish`).

skills.name: game-ui-ux
skills.description: Engine-neutral design rules for game HUDs and menus: anchors and containers, scaling, safe areas, gamepad focus, HUDs driven by events instead of polling, and accessibility minimums. Use for menus, health bars or inventory screens that break on ultrawide or phones. Pair with `godot-ui-control` or `roblox-ui`. Not for button juice (`game-feel`) or rebinding (`input-systems`).

skills.name: godot-csharp
skills.description: C# and .NET in Godot 4.7: partial node classes, the PascalCase lifecycle, [Export] and [Signal], signals as C# events, the .csproj and calling GDScript. Use for .cs scripts in Godot, porting GDScript to C#, a failed build, or a failed web or Android export. Not for GDScript (`godot-gdscript`), Unity C# (`unity-csharp-scripting`) or export presets (`godot-export`).

skills.name: godot-export
skills.description: Exports Godot 4.7 projects: templates, export_presets.cfg for desktop, Web and Android, command-line exports and web COOP/COEP headers. Use on "No export template found", a blank web build, a SharedArrayBuffer error or files missing after export. Not for tests in CI (`godot-gdscript-headless-testing`), store uploads (`steam-publish`, `itch-publish`) or netcode (`godot-multiplayer`).

skills.name: godot-gdscript-headless-testing
skills.description: Runs Godot 4.7 GDScript tests with godot --headless and a SceneTree runner that exits non-zero on failure, so CI can gate merges. Owns Godot tests in CI. Use for GitHub Actions jobs or a headless run that hangs or exits 0 despite SCRIPT ERROR lines. Not for export in CI (`godot-export`), GDScript language (`godot-gdscript`) or Unity tests (`unity-csharp-scripting`).

skills.name: godot-multiplayer
skills.description: Godot 4.7 high-level multiplayer: ENet host and join, @rpc with rpc_id(), MultiplayerSpawner and MultiplayerSynchronizer, with a two-instance headless test. Use for online or LAN co-op in Godot, or a rejected RPC, spawned nodes missing on clients, or state that does not sync. Not for Roblox (`roblox-networking`), server exports (`godot-export`) or local split-screen (`camera-systems`).

skills.name: godot-physics
skills.description: Godot 4.7 physics API in 2D and 3D: body and Area types, collision_layer and mask bits, Area signals for hurtboxes, RayCast and space queries, and Jolt (3D default since 4.6). Use when objects pass through each other, body_entered never fires or a raycast hits itself. Not for engine-neutral jitter and tunnelling (`physics-tuning`) or CharacterBody movement (`godot-2d-movement`).

skills.name: godot-resources
skills.description: Godot 4.7 data-driven design with custom Resources: class_name and @export fields, .tres files, shared references vs duplicate_deep(), uids and threaded loading. Use for items, stats or enemy configs as data, or when editing one enemy changes every enemy or a .tres stops loading. Not for save slots (`save-systems`) or the C# version (`godot-csharp`).

skills.name: godot-shaders
skills.description: Godot 4.7 Shading Language syntax and pipeline: canvas_item, spatial and particle shaders, built-ins, ShaderMaterial wiring, a headless compile check and 3.x porting. Use for a .gdshader, a SHADER ERROR, shader parameters set from GDScript, or an effect that looks washed out or sorts wrong. Not for effect maths such as dissolve or outline (`shader-programming`).

skills.name: godot-signals-groups
skills.description: Godot 4.7 signals and node groups: typed signals, connect() with Callables, one-shot and deferred connections, event-bus autoloads and call_group broadcasts. Use when nodes must talk without hard references, a handler fires twice or never, or the log says "already connected". Not for GDScript syntax (`godot-gdscript`) or autoload setup (`godot-nodes-scenes`).

skills.name: godot-tilemap

plugins.name: goose-skills
plugins.description: 124 skills for growth and go-to-market: running ads, social, content, lead generation, SEO and data scraping.
plugins.author: Gooseworks
exampleQueries: Plan an ad campaign for this product
Scrape data for a market report

skills.name: ad-angle-miner
skills.description: Research supported advertising promises from a specific buyer's context, current product facts, customer language and observed ads. Turn them into static, video or copy ideas; match video ideas to actual recipes and save a product-scoped angle bank for write-video-ad-script. Product-led discovery can use verified facts without reviews. Reference persistence and reach are observations, not proof of performance.

skills.name: ad-lead-quality-analyzer
skills.description: For paid lead-gen and participant-recruitment ads, replaces vanity CPA with true CAC per qualified lead by joining ad-platform data with downstream funnel events, surfaces tracking gaps, and classifies every creative into Scale / Keep / Investigate / Cut.

skills.name: ad-management-intake
skills.description: The intake stage of a Meta ad harness. Researches the brand first, states what it assumes, and asks only what it cannot infer and what would change money, claims or legal exposure if guessed wrong — at most four questions a turn, in plain business language. Writes the brand's stable facts (ads/brand.md), the campaign brief, and a log of what was asked vs assumed. Use it when someone wants to run Meta ads and the brand's ad facts are not yet recorded.

skills.name: ad-policy-check
skills.description: Checks paid ads against the ad platform's rules (Meta, TikTok, Google, LinkedIn and others) and the brand's category rules: the copy, on-image or on-screen text, pictures and people. Rewrites what can be fixed honestly, adds the disclosures that are needed, and flags anything that needs a human or legal review, with one pass, fixed or flag line per ad and platform. Use alone when you already have the ad text or images and know where they will run; otherwise run the playbook for the job (e.g. make-static-ads, make-content, email-lifecycle).

skills.name: ads-north-star-strategy
skills.description: Turn a brand's facts, a campaign brief and the product into a one-minute Meta ad strategy with its reasoning — goal, audience, objective and placements, budget split, how many ads and how different they must be (generate 3x so the user can choose), the test frame, the success metric, and safety rules for the user to accept. Decides what launch-meta-ad-campaign then executes, and re-reads the strategy after a deep check to show which assumption changed. Use it after intake and before any creative is generated or any campaign is built.

skills.name: analyze-performance
skills.description: Weekly performance read across every channel we run: what worked, why, and what to make next, judged on the business's real number (store revenue, qualified pipeline, retained users), not platform claims. Use when: write my Monday report; how are my ads doing — which ad won?; are my ads actually making money (Meta says 4x ROAS but revenue is flat); why did sales drop this week; did the test win; is my tracking working; monthly numbers for the replan; anything on fire today. Not for acting on the recommendations (pausing, scaling, launching) — use run-paid-campaigns; not for replanning the budget — use plan-campaign.

skills.name: analyze-performance-call-and-learn
skills.description: Step of the analyze-performance playbook: calls ended tests, scores last week's calls, writes this week's kill/scale/hold calls and drafts learnings for the brand brain. Run analyze-performance instead; not for direct use.

skills.name: analyze-performance-diagnose
skills.description: Step of the analyze-performance playbook: flags tracking breaks with fixes and explains each big metric move with evidence, confidence and ruled-out causes. Run analyze-performance instead; not for direct use.

skills.name: analyze-performance-intake
skills.description: Step of the analyze-performance playbook: gathers the week's numbers from tools, exports and pastes, cleans them, and writes the coverage line or switches to claims-only mode. Run analyze-performance instead; not for direct use.

skills.name: analyze-performance-rank-and-read
skills.description: Step of the analyze-performance playbook: ranks creative by angle, hook and format with spend gates, writes short per-channel reads and drafts what to make next. Run analyze-performance instead; not for direct use.

skills.name: analyze-performance-revenue-join
skills.description: Step of the analyze-performance playbook: joins cleaned store or CRM numbers with ad spend to build the business-truth table, MER, new-customer cost and the overclaim ratio. Run analyze-performance instead; not for direct use.

skills.name: animate-image
skills.description: Animate an existing product image or static ad into a short branded video using the GooseWorks Animate Images workflow, with source-image continuity and optional end-frame control.

skills.name: answer-ads-questions
skills.description: Answer questions about a brand's Meta ads (spend, results, which ad is winning, is it paused, why did Goose do that) only from reads made in the same turn, with the data window and sync time on every number and a plain caveat when the connection is stale or partial. Use it whenever a user asks how their ads are doing or why an ad action was taken.

skills.name: claims-gate
skills.description: Checks every claim in a piece of copy (ads, emails, posts, pages, scripts, briefs) against the claims the brand has approved. Keeps, rewrites or cuts each line, and lists the proof that would bring a cut line back. When a line the copy needs has no approval, it asks for a short sign-off on the 3 or 4 lines that matter and records the answer. Use alone when you already have the copy and a brand set up; otherwise run the playbook for the job (e.g. make-static-ads, make-content, write-outreach).

skills.name: comment-mining
skills.description: Mine comments and replies on social posts, videos, and ads for recurring customer language, questions, objections, desired outcomes, complaints, product requests, purchase signals, and creative opportunities. Use for voice-of-customer research grounded in linked source evidence.

skills.name: company-contact-finder
skills.description: Find decision-makers at a specific company using Fiber, Crustdata and PDL people search inside the GooseWorks coworker. Given a company name and target titles, returns a list of contacts with name, title, LinkedIn URL, and location.

skills.name: create-kinetic-typography
skills.description: Render a deterministic text-only video ad from approved copy, font, colors, timing and CTA. Use when a brand needs an animated message without product photography or a creator.

skills.name: email-lifecycle
skills.description: Lifecycle email, SMS and push: audits the list and deliverability, then writes the flows this kind of business needs first, loadable as-is in your own tool, plus segments, cadence and this week's broadcasts. Never sends anything. Use when: set up my welcome and abandoned-cart emails; trial onboarding or waitlist launch emails; win back lapsed customers; plan this week's emails and texts; push notifications for my app; why are my emails going to spam; plan our Black Friday email and SMS sends; a send went wrong. Not for cold outreach to prospects — use write-outreach; not the editorial newsletter issue — use make-content; not the whole cross-channel Black Friday plan — use plan-campaign.

skills.name: email-lifecycle-broadcast-planner
skills.description: Step of the email-lifecycle playbook: builds the month's send calendar and writes this week's email and SMS broadcasts against the approved cadence and segments. Run email-lifecycle instead; not for direct use.

skills.name: email-lifecycle-flow-writer
skills.description: Step of the email-lifecycle playbook: writes one lifecycle flow as a build sheet for the brand's email tool, every message finished in the brand voice. Run email-lifecycle instead; not for direct use.

skills.name: email-lifecycle-lifecycle-audit
skills.description: Step of the email-lifecycle playbook: audits list, consent, live flows, recent sends and sending setup, marking every item verified, from-you or unknown. Run email-lifecycle instead; not for direct use.

skills.name: email-lifecycle-offer-math
skills.description: Prices one discount, free-shipping threshold or referral reward against contribution margin: cost per order, share of margin used, break-even lift, code leakage risks, and one recommended offer in two plain sentences. Use alone when you already have the offer, average order value and margin per product; otherwise run email-lifecycle.

skills.name: email-lifecycle-send-check
skills.description: Checks a drafted email flow or broadcast before it is loaded: flow logic and exits, overlaps, offer depth and codes, stock, claims, consent and legal footer, SMS rules, rendering, voice and AI-copy tells, and the goal metric. Returns a pass / fixed / open-question table. Use alone when you already have the finished draft and the brand's product and policy facts; otherwise run email-lifecycle.

skills.name: get-brand-assets
skills.description: Get company logos, brand colors, fonts, and style guides

skills.name: goose-ads
skills.description: Edit, resize, animate and study image ads with GooseWorks in this chat. New static or image ads go to the make-static-ads skill when it is installed or catalog_fetch opens it. Read the brand and follow the active playbook, preserving factual prerequisites and approvals.

skills.name: goose-graphics-create-format
skills.description: Creates a new graphics format spec (custom canvas dimensions + content rules) and publishes it to the Gooseworks library so any agent can render against it. Use when the existing community formats (carousel, story, infographic, slides, poster, chart, tweet, plus community additions) don't fit the user's canvas — e.g., LinkedIn banner 1584×396, story cover 1080×1920, event flyer 8.5×11in. Mirrors goose-graphics-create-style but for formats.

skills.name: goose-graphics-create-style
skills.description: End-to-end skill that turns a single reference image into a published Gooseworks style — analyzes the image, drafts the slim style spec, renders a hero example plus 2-3 additional formats via Playwright, writes the `gooseworks-style.json` manifest, and publishes via `npx gooseworks styles publish` so other agents can discover it. Mirrors goose-graphics-create-format but for styles.

skills.name: goose-product-photos
skills.description: Make product photos (studio, lifestyle or on a model) of a brand's real products with GooseWorks in this chat. Start brand work with brand_knowledge_browse and follow the next_step in every answer.

skills.name: goose-video
skills.description: Make a video ad in this chat from a real reference ad, found or theirs; styles are the fallback. Follow every answer's next_step.

skills.name: goose-video-local
skills.description: Make an approved GooseWorks video when an answer's next_step gives its command.

skills.name: gooseworks
skills.description: GooseWorks growth coworker and router for markets, competitors, audiences, creators, campaigns, ads, photos, graphics, video, content, email, SEO, social, leads and contacts. Use for brand facts or copy too, so offers, prices, rules, audience and bestsellers reach the brand's Marketing Brain.

skills.name: honest-review
skills.description: Shared step of the marketing playbooks (make-static-ads, run-organic-social): how to review generated images and video honestly. Covers what was seen by eye versus read automatically, findings framed as things for the human to confirm, remakes only after a yes to the price, and at most two tries per item. Loaded by those playbooks; not for direct use.

skills.name: improve-search-visibility-citation-check
skills.description: Step of the improve-search-visibility playbook: runs the agreed buyer questions on AI and Google surfaces, records every run and scores how often the brand is named. Run improve-search-visibility instead; not for direct use.

skills.name: improve-search-visibility-entity-footprint
skills.description: Step of the improve-search-visibility playbook: checks the profiles answer engines read, plus local listings and reviews, against the brand's facts and writes corrections. Run improve-search-visibility instead; not for direct use.

skills.name: improve-search-visibility-fix-writer
skills.description: Step of the improve-search-visibility playbook: turns one ranked fix into paste-ready site copy or code with owner, risk and undo, and writes page briefs. Run improve-search-visibility instead; not for direct use.

skills.name: improve-search-visibility-page-and-foundation-check
skills.description: Step of the improve-search-visibility playbook: audits site indexing, crawling, technical and page issues at the requested scope, or checks pages behind lost visibility questions. Run improve-search-visibility instead; not for direct use.

skills.name: improve-search-visibility-question-set
skills.description: Step of the improve-search-visibility playbook: drafts and scores the buyer-question set in AI and Google forms and groups it into page clusters. Run improve-search-visibility instead; not for direct use.

skills.name: improve-search-visibility-store-listing-audit
skills.description: Audits an app's App Store and Google Play listing against three competitors (title, subtitle, description opening, first screenshots and captions, rating, review themes) and writes a field-by-field rewrite with character counts, or a launch-day listing before release. Use alone when you already have the app's store links and signed-off product facts; otherwise run improve-search-visibility.

skills.name: learn-my-brand
skills.description: Learn my brand once and stop asking me every time. Use when someone says learn my brand, set up my brand, here's our brand book, remember how we talk, what can we claim, can we say this, approve our claims, sign off our voice, our price or product changed, the client approved the claims, pick up where we left off, or check our claims are still current. Reads what GooseWorks already found about the brand, asks only the gaps as drafts to confirm, audits every claim (including ones research marked approved) and gets the ones that matter signed off with proof, scope and review date, turns the voice into rules the owner confirms, checks logo, colours and fonts, and saves it all as it goes so every other job loads it instead of asking. Ends with an unknowns list and a read-back. Not for who our customers are and what they say (use research-audience) or writing positioning from scratch (not covered yet).

skills.name: make-content
skills.description: Writes marketing content: articles, single posts, newsletters, scripts and repurposed cuts, each with an edit note and a claims check. Use when a marketer says "write a blog post / case study", "write a LinkedIn or X post / thread / X article", "carousel copy", "draft this week's newsletter", "turn this webinar into posts" or "repurpose this", "write a TikTok or YouTube script", "refresh this old post", or "write the page from this SEO brief". Words only; nothing is invented or published. Not for a dated posting calendar — use run-organic-social; not ad copy (make-static-ads) or promo emails (email-lifecycle). Press releases, landing and product pages, and sales decks are not covered.

skills.name: make-content-content-brief
skills.description: Writes a one-page content brief before any draft: audience, intent, the one arguable point, what top results already say and what this piece adds, an outline, a proof inventory with gaps marked, voice, CTA and banned words, checked against six gates. Use alone when you already have the topic, format, audience and destination and want only the brief; otherwise run make-content.

skills.name: make-content-source-to-units
skills.description: Step of the make-content playbook: mines one finished asset into scored quotable units and maps a different lead unit to each platform. Run make-content instead; not for direct use.

skills.name: make-content-two-pass-edit
skills.description: Edits an existing draft in order: a substance pass (arguable thesis, swap test, fakes removed, CTA fit), a claims and fact check that cuts or softens unproven lines, a readability and voice-match pass, then an AI-tell sweep, with an edit note listing open gaps. Use alone when you already have a finished draft and the brand's voice samples and approved claims; otherwise run make-content.

skills.name: make-custom-video
skills.description: Create a custom video with sourced product accuracy, explicit sound routing and exact-final audiovisual review.

skills.name: make-product-photos
skills.description: Use when the marketer says: studio photos of my product without a shoot, product photos for my store page, packshots on white, lifestyle or on-model shots, photos for the new colourway, fresh product imagery for ads, photos for our launch page, our packaging changed — redo the photos, I have no photographer. Delivers store-ready product photos generated from the brand's real product photos: a shot list built from the page slots (hero, alt angle, scale, detail, in use, lifestyle, on-model), only real photos of this product as references, matched to the brand's photography, every shot checked against the real product for shape, parts, logo, text, colour, finish, scale and honest representation, with a keep / maybe / reject verdict and a page order. The human picks the keepers. Never uploads to a store, never shows a size, part, feature or result the product lacks. Not for ads with text, infographics or screenshots — make-static-ads; not for marketplace listing sets (not covered yet).

skills.name: make-static-ads-ad-copy
skills.description: Step of make-static-ads: writes the text for each slot the ad's template sets, then the primary texts, headline, description and CTA around the image, from usable facts and customer words. Run make-static-ads instead; not for direct use.

skills.name: make-static-ads-claims-extract
skills.description: Step of the make-static-ads playbook: pulls every claim-bearing span out of an ad — the copy around the image, the on-image words in the prompt, badges, and what the picture implies — and keeps or cuts each by the brand-brain rule. Runs before spend on the finished prompt (Pass A) and on every render (Pass B). Run make-static-ads instead; not for direct use.

skills.name: make-static-ads-compose
skills.description: Step of make-static-ads: writes each ad's render prompt and ordered image list from its concept-board row, one per ad and ratio, ready for a quoted render. Run make-static-ads instead; not for direct use.

skills.name: make-static-ads-concept-grid
skills.description: Step of make-static-ads: turns the chosen angles into messages, visual ideas and a template per ad, checks each against the brand profile and recent ads, writes the concept board and has a fresh critic attack it before any copy, prompt or spend. Run make-static-ads instead; not for direct use.

skills.name: make-static-ads-copy-variants
skills.description: Step of the make-static-ads playbook: after an image is approved, makes more versions of the same picture with different hooks, headlines or fonts by a quoted re-render with the approved render attached as the brand's own image, so copy can be tested without new visuals. Offered, never default. Run make-static-ads instead; not for direct use.

skills.name: make-static-ads-find-references
skills.description: Step of make-static-ads: picks a template for every ad in its chosen style, after its visual idea and style are set, from the brand's own ads, the GooseWorks library or category leaders, and records what the chosen creativity level keeps from it. Run make-static-ads instead; not for direct use.

skills.name: make-static-ads-fix-rejected
skills.description: Step of the make-static-ads playbook: fixes a static image ad the platform rejected — finds the ad, maps the platform's reason to the line or element at fault, fixes copy for free or re-composes the image text on a quote, re-runs the claims and policy checks, and answers the request. A rejected video is the video playbook's job. Run make-static-ads instead; not for direct use.

skills.name: make-static-ads-graphic-request
skills.description: Makes one simple non-ad brand graphic, such as an email header, social feed or story image, or a blog or link-preview image, in the brand's style with at most a short line of text, after claim and rights checks and a yes to the quote; returns the link and alt text. Not for carousels, decks or print. Use alone when you already have the purpose, placement and exact wording; otherwise run make-static-ads.

skills.name: make-static-ads-render-review
skills.description: Step of make-static-ads: a fresh judge checks every render against its concept-board row and the official product photos, one retry inside the marketer's approval, then the claims and set checks; records each verdict in tags and the batch file. Run make-static-ads instead; not for direct use.

skills.name: make-video-ads
skills.description: Use when the marketer says: make me a video ad, a 30-second ad for paid social, a Reel / TikTok / Shorts ad, a UGC-style video made with AI (no real creator), a product demo video, remake this ad I like for my brand, cut our best organic video into an ad, more like my winning video with new hooks, my video ad got rejected — fix it. Delivers a produced, ready-to-post video ad grounded in a researched angle: one message, a hook for the first two seconds, every claim traced to the brand's signed-off claims, no generated person posing as a customer, the exact words and the price approved before anything renders (one video, or one plus two hook variants), an honest review of the result, priced fixes only on a yes, and launch copy and notes for the ads team. Works in chat apps. Never publishes or spends ad budget. Not for real creators filming for you — work-with-creators (unsure? ask: AI-made or a real person); not for a phone-shot organic post — run-organic-social; not for static ads — make-static-ads.

skills.name: marketing-data-access

skills.name: mirrord-beyond
skills.description: Help users set up and use mirrord Beyond, which runs a local process against workloads outside Kubernetes (docs section "Beyond Kubernetes"; the CLI, dashboard and config call them serverless workloads and `serverless/` targets). Two tracks. ECS setup, for platform teams - wire an existing Amazon ECS service (Fargate or EC2) to the MetalBear Cloud sessions-manager - store the serverless agent API key in AWS Secrets Manager, merge the mirrord remote bootstrap into the task definition, deploy and verify. Developer session - sign in with `mirrord login`, write a `mirrord-up.yaml` with a `serverless/` target, and run `mirrord up` (or the IDE) against the ECS service. Use when users mention mirrord Beyond, Beyond Kubernetes, ECS or Fargate with mirrord, serverless targets, sessions-manager, MetalBear Cloud, the serverless agent API key, MIRRORD_REMOTE_SERVICE, or errors from either side. Also covers the Operator-hosted mode briefly.

skills.name: mirrord-chaos
skills.description: Help users chaos test their app with mirrord: inject artificial latency or connection errors into a mirrord session's outgoing traffic via per-session chaos rules managed with the `mirrord chaos` CLI. Use when a user wants to add latency or delay to outgoing connections or a dependency (e.g. a slow database), simulate connection failures (reset, timed out, refused), test app behavior under degraded network conditions, or wire chaos rules into CI test runs. Always use this skill instead of the deprecated _experimental_.latency mirrord config option.

skills.name: mirrord-config
skills.description: Helps users generate, edit, and validate mirrord.json configuration files for mirrord (MetalBear). Use when the user wants to connect their local process to a Kubernetes environment, configure features (env/fs/network), or needs feedback on an existing mirrord.json. Always ensures output JSON is valid and schema-conformant.

skills.name: mirrord-db-branching
skills.description: Helps users configure mirrord.json for database branching, enabling isolated database copies for safe development and testing. Use when the user wants to set up MySQL, MariaDB, PostgreSQL, MSSQL, MongoDB, Redis, DynamoDB, ClickHouse, Google Spanner, Amazon S3, turbopuffer, or generic branches, configure copy modes, connection sources, schema migrations, IAM authentication, or manage database branches.

skills.name: mirrord-header-propagation
skills.description: Makes a codebase propagate W3C baggage (the `baggage` header carrying `mirrord-session=<key>`) end to end, so mirrord HTTP filters, preview environments, and queue splitting can route a whole request chain to one developer's session. Detects existing OpenTelemetry, Datadog, or other tracing that can already propagate baggage and enables it; otherwise adds a small propagation layer. Covers inbound/outbound HTTP and gRPC, publishing to and consuming from Kafka, RabbitMQ, SQS/SNS, GCP Pub/Sub, Azure Service Bus, NATS, Redis Pub/Sub, BullMQ and Temporal, per-message context restore in consumers, and storage hand-offs such as a GCS signed URL upload that triggers Pub/Sub or an S3 presigned upload that triggers SQS. Ends with a report of every flow found and which ones still drop the header. Use when the user asks to propagate headers, baggage, tracestate, the mirrord session key, or trace context across services or queues, or when a mirrord filter matches the first service but not downstream services or queue consumers.

skills.name: mirrord-kafka
skills.description: Helps DevOps engineers configure mirrord Operator's Kafka queue splitting feature end-to-end. Generates the MirrordSplitConfig and MirrordPropertyList Kubernetes CRD YAMLs (the current resources; MirrordKafkaTopicsConsumer + MirrordKafkaClientConfig are deprecated but still supported), the matching mirrord.json split_queues section with message_filter and jq_filter, and Helm value guidance. Use this skill whenever the user mentions Kafka splitting with mirrord, MirrordSplitConfig, MirrordPropertyList, MirrordKafkaClientConfig, MirrordKafkaTopicsConsumer, Kafka queue/topic splitting, configuring mirrord with Kafka, Kafka Streams splitting, MSK IAM auth, or troubleshooting Kafka splitting sessions. Also trigger on split_queues with queue_type Kafka, or connecting mirrord to a Kafka cluster. This is a Team/Enterprise feature of mirrord.

skills.name: mirrord-operator
skills.description: Help users install and configure the mirrord Operator for team/enterprise environments. Use when users ask about operator setup, Helm installation, cloud API key or license configuration, air-gapped/offline licensing, enabling features (queue splitting, DB branching, preview environments, multi-cluster), internal registries, OpenShift/GKE Autopilot, RBAC, or multi-user mirrord deployments. Also use when an AI agent hits a Team or Enterprise feature on a cluster with no license and needs to offer the user a trial (agent-started trial; the trial is Enterprise tier).

skills.description: Guide users from zero to their first working mirrord session — check system requirements, install mirrord via CLI, VS Code, or IntelliJ, run a first session against a Kubernetes target, and verify the connection. Use when a user is new to mirrord, wants to install it, needs help running their first session, or wants to debug or test a local process against their Kubernetes cluster.

skills.name: mirrord-temporal
skills.description: Helps DevOps engineers configure mirrord Operator's Temporal task queue splitting feature end-to-end. plugins.description: Eighteen skills for open science: running and reproducing research, and the tools that make it possible.

exampleQueries: Reproduce this analysis
Set up this research project

skills.name: alphafold2
skills.description: Predict protein structure for monomers and multimers with AlphaFold2 via the ColabFold runner (Mirdita et al. 2022, github.com/sokrypton/ColabFold; AlphaFold2 Jumper et al. 2021). Reach for this skill to fold a sequence or complex with the AF2/AF2-Multimer evoformer, to validate designed sequences by self-consistency pLDDT, ipTM, and RMSD, or to run a quick MSA-backed prediction using the public MMseqs2 server.

skills.name: boltz
skills.description: Structure prediction for protein, nucleic-acid, and small-molecule complexes with Boltz-2 (Passaro & Wohlwend et al. 2025, github.com/jwohlwend/boltz). Reach for this skill to validate designed binders against a target, to co-fold a protein with a SMILES or CCD ligand, or to get an open-source AlphaFold3 alternative with optional binding-affinity prediction.

skills.name: borzoi
skills.description: Predict genome-wide functional tracks (RNA-seq, CAGE, DNase, ChIP) from DNA sequence with Borzoi. Use this skill when: (1) Scoring the regulatory effect of a variant on expression/accessibility, (2) Generating predicted coverage tracks for a locus, (3) Prioritising non-coding variants by predicted track delta.

skills.name: chai1
skills.description: Structure prediction for protein, nucleic-acid, and small-molecule complexes with the Chai-1 foundation model (Chai Discovery 2024, github.com/chaidiscovery/chai-lab). Reach for this skill to predict an antibody-antigen or protein-ligand complex from a single FASTA, to re-fold designed binders as an AlphaFold-multimer alternative, or to drive co-folding from Python for batched campaigns on a GPU.

skills.name: compute-env-setup
skills.description: Prepare reproducible setup instructions and validate a user-managed named software environment on an Open-Science SSH Compute Host, including direct SSH and Slurm hosts. Use when a remote job needs packages, modules, cache variables, or a repeatable activation that the host does not already provide.

skills.name: customize
skills.description: Use when the user wants to create or manage a Specialist agent or create, revise, publish, or delete a Skill through the conversational `/Customize` entry. Routes Skill work to the internal skill-creator and handles Specialist work through the JavaScript host.agents SDK.

skills.name: diffdock
skills.description: Predict small-molecule binding poses with DiffDock-L (Corso et al. 2023/2024, github.com/gcorso/DiffDock) — blind diffusion docking that places a ligand into a protein pocket without a predefined search box and ranks the samples with a learned confidence model. Reach for this skill to dock a SMILES or SDF against a PDB, to generate ranked 3D poses for a small fragment library, or to get a starting pose for downstream rescoring. DiffDock predicts geometry, not affinity.

skills.name: esmfold2
skills.description: Biohub ESMFold2 / ESMFold2-Fast all-atom co-folding (Candido et al. 2026, github.com/Biohub/esm). Single-sequence and MSA modes; protein, DNA, RNA, ligand (CCD/SMILES), modified residues. FoldBench Ab-Ag 50-55%, PPI 70-77% DockQ-pass. Also covers the ESMC-{300M,600M,6B} protein language models from the same release: masked-LM logits, hidden states, mutation scoring, contact prediction, and the SAE interpretability head. MIT-licensed weights on HuggingFace org `biohub`. Use this skill when: (1) Predicting complex structures with single-sequence input, (2) Validating designed binders with ESMFold2-Fast, (3) Running ESMFold2 with MSA input, (4) Getting ESMC embeddings or per-residue mutation scores, (5) Choosing kernel backend and sampling-step settings for paper-faithful throughput.

skills.name: evo2
skills.description: Score, embed, and generate DNA sequences with Evo 2, a long-context genomic foundation model. Use this skill when: (1) Computing per-nucleotide or per-sequence likelihoods for variant effect scoring, (2) Embedding genomic windows for downstream classification, (3) Generating DNA conditioned on a prefix, (4) Scoring regulatory or coding regions across species.

skills.name: fair-esm2
skills.description: Embed proteins with Meta AI's ESM-2 (`fair-esm` package). Use this skill when: (1) Extracting per-residue or per-sequence embeddings for downstream ML, (2) Masked-LM likelihood / mutation effect scoring, (3) Contact prediction from a sequence.

skills.name: indication-dossier
skills.description: Generate a therapeutic indication dossier. Covers the patient population, epidemiology, disease biology, standard of care, regulatory precedent, and landmark clinical trials.

skills.name: ligandmpnn
skills.description: Inverse-fold a backbone with ligand, nucleic-acid, and metal context using LigandMPNN (Dauparas et al. 2023, github.com/dauparas/LigandMPNN). Reach for this skill to redesign the residues lining a binding pocket around a bound small molecule or cofactor, to design metal-coordinating sites where the geometry must be respected, or to get threaded designed-sequence PDBs out of any MPNN run.

skills.name: openfold3
skills.description: Structure prediction using OpenFold3, an open-weights PyTorch reproduction of AlphaFold3 from the AlQuraishi Lab. Use this skill when predicting protein/nucleic-acid/ligand complex structures with an Apache-2.0-licensed AF3 reimplementation.

skills.name: proteinmpnn
skills.description: Inverse-fold a protein backbone (PDB structure) into amino-acid sequence with ProteinMPNN (Dauparas et al. 2022, github.com/dauparas/ProteinMPNN). Reach for this skill to run sequence design on RFdiffusion backbones, to redesign one chain of a PDB while holding interface residues fixed, or to generate a temperature-swept set of sequences for downstream folding.

skills.name: remote-compute-ssh
skills.description: Evaluate and use Remote Compute before choosing where to run GPU, high-memory, parallel, batch, model-inference, bioinformatics, or other long-running scientific work; supports short remote commands and asynchronous jobs with automatic harvest and analysis.

skills.name: scgpt
skills.description: Embed and annotate single-cell expression data with scGPT, a foundation model for single-cell biology. Use this skill when: (1) Producing cell embeddings from an AnnData for clustering/integration, (2) Zero-shot or fine-tuned cell-type annotation, (3) Gene-level representation for perturbation/GRN tasks. For probabilistic single-cell models (scVI etc.), use the scvi-tools library.

skills.name: self-awareness
skills.description: Inspect Open-Science's JavaScript control REPL, discover managed Project files, Sessions, and Agent Frames, and safely feature-gate host.* calls with host.capabilities(). Use when an Agent needs to discover available host APIs, locate an Artifact or Upload Version, diagnose a Session, or read a Frame transcript in the current Project.

skills.name: solublempnn
skills.description: Inverse-fold a backbone with SolubleMPNN — ProteinMPNN retrained on a soluble-PDB subset (Dauparas et al. 2022) — for sequences biased toward cytosolic expression and reduced aggregation. Reach for this skill when designs from vanilla ProteinMPNN are aggregating or going to inclusion bodies, when redesigning a membrane-adjacent fold for soluble expression, or when an E. coli expression screen is the next step.
